best_for: Colorists wanting to master node-based grading
Editors looking to switch from Premiere Pro or Final Cut
Filmmakers wanting an all-in-one post-production solution
not_for: Those who only want to edit simple social media reels
target_audience.who_should_take_foundation_first: Absolute beginners should take Professional Video Editing first to understand basic timelines.

prerequisites.required: Basic understanding of video editing concepts and color theory.
prerequisites.recommended: Prior experience editing video in any NLE.

system_requirements.hardware: Multi-core processor, 16GB RAM minimum (32GB recommended), Dedicated GPU with at least 4GB VRAM.

overview.positioning: The ultimate guide to the industry's most powerful all-in-one post-production software.
overview.short_description: Master editing, cinematic color grading, Fusion VFX, and Fairlight audio mixing entirely within DaVinci Resolve.

key_facts.ai_integration: Resolve Studio Neural Engine features (Magic Mask, Voice Isolation)

what_you_will_be_able_to_do: Edit fast-paced sequences using the Cut and Edit pages
Grade RAW and Log footage using node trees and power windows
Create basic motion graphics and VFX in the Fusion page
Mix broadcast-compliant audio in the Fairlight page

why_now.industry_shift: DaVinci Resolve has taken over the industry, shifting from just a color grading tool to the primary NLE for many studios and YouTubers.
why_now.ai_impact: Resolve's Neural Engine features (like Magic Mask and Depth Map) allow solo creators to achieve Hollywood-level rotoscoping and grading in seconds.
why_now.business_demand: High demand for dedicated Colorists and Finishing Artists in commercial and film production.
why_now.career_opportunity: Node-based grading is a premium skill that commands significantly higher rates than standard editing.

learning_outcomes: EDIT: Navigate the Cut and Edit pages for rapid assembly.
COLOR: Build professional node trees for color correction and cinematic grading.
COMPOSITE: Use Fusion for node-based VFX, tracking, and titles.
MIX: Utilize Fairlight for dialogue cleanup and sound design.

stages.focus: Media management, the Cut page, and the Edit page.
Color management, primary correction, and node-based grading.
Fusion node compositing and Fairlight audio mixing.

core_tools.what_student_learns: Node trees, qualifiers, curves, power windows, and LUTs.
EQ, compression, dialogue isolation, and mixing.

emerging_tools.purpose: AI Magic Mask and Voice Isolation (Studio version).

industry_workflow.overview: The standard DaVinci Resolve finishing pipeline.

stages.name: Media/Conform
stages.desc: Importing XMLs from Premiere or assembling footage.

stages.name: Edit
stages.desc: Locking the picture sequence in the Edit page.

stages.name: Color
stages.desc: Primary balance and secondary stylized grading.

stages.name: Fusion & Fairlight
stages.desc: VFX polish and final audio mix.

stages.name: Deliver
stages.desc: Exporting master files and web-optimized formats.

business_use_cases.business_problem: Raw footage looks flat and lacks emotional impact.

ai_integration.ai_can_assist_with: Isolating subjects for grading (Magic Mask), fixing bad audio (Voice Isolation).
ai_integration.ai_can_automate: Color matching shots and upscaling resolution.
ai_integration.ai_cannot_replace: The creative intent of the color grade or the storytelling of the edit.
ai_integration.human_expertise_required: Understanding color theory and emotional tone.
ai_integration.validation_protocol: Checking scopes to ensure broadcast safe colors.

best_practices: Always use a structured node tree (e.g., NR -> Primary -> Secondary -> Look).
Rely on scopes (Waveform, Vectorscope) rather than just your monitor.
Use Color Management (RCM or ACES) for accurate starting points.

common_mistakes.why_it_happens: Rushing to apply a LUT or 'look'.
common_mistakes.professional_approach: Always balance exposure and white balance in the primary nodes before applying creative grades.

career_paths.employer_expectations: Deep understanding of nodes, scopes, and color management.
career_paths.what_student_demonstrates: A before/after color grading reel showing various cinematic looks.

freelance_applications.client_workflow: Receive XML/Timeline -> Conform -> Grade -> Review -> Render

final_deliverables: A comprehensive before/after color grading showreel.

assessment.criteria: Skin tone accuracy, shot matching, node structure efficiency, and narrative flow.

faq.question: Do I need the Studio (Paid) version of Resolve?
faq.answer: No, the free version is incredibly powerful and covers 95% of what we teach, though AI features like Magic Mask require Studio.

modules.module_purpose: Understand the page-based workflow and master the Cut and Edit pages.

lessons.what_is_taught: Databases vs Project files, importing media, and generating proxies.
lessons.why_it_matters: Resolve manages files differently than Premiere; understanding databases prevents lost work.
lessons.what_learner_does: Creates a database and organizes footage bins.

lessons.what_is_taught: Three-point editing, trimming tools, and the Inspector panel.
lessons.why_it_matters: The core of non-linear editing in Resolve.
lessons.what_learner_does: Cuts together a short interview sequence.

lessons.what_is_taught: Importing XMLs from Premiere/FCP and relinking media.
lessons.why_it_matters: Essential for colorists working with external editors.
lessons.what_learner_does: Conforms an XML timeline and fixes offline clips.
lessons.expected_outcome: A timeline ready for the Color page.

modules.hands_on_practice: Assemble and trim a narrative sequence.

modules.module_purpose: Learn the industry-standard node workflow for color correction and grading.

lessons.what_is_taught: Setting up Resolve Color Management, reading Waveforms and Vectorscopes.
lessons.why_it_matters: Ensures accurate translation of Log/RAW footage to Rec.709 displays.
lessons.what_learner_does: Normalizes Log footage using RCM and balances exposure.

lessons.what_is_taught: Using Lift/Gamma/Gain wheels, curves, and matching clips in a scene.
lessons.why_it_matters: If shots don't match, the audience is distracted from the story.
lessons.what_learner_does: Matches three different camera angles to look identical.

lessons.what_is_taught: Isolating skin tones, drawing masks, and tracking.
lessons.why_it_matters: Allows specific stylized adjustments without affecting the whole image.
lessons.what_learner_does: Isolates a subject's face, brightens it, and tracks the movement.
lessons.expected_outcome: A professional, stylized shot with perfect skin tones.

modules.hands_on_practice: Color correct and grade a multi-shot sequence.
modules.expected_outcome: Ability to execute a professional node-based color grade.

modules.module_purpose: Add VFX, mix audio, and deliver the final master file.
what_you_will_learn: Audio mixing and EQ in Fairlight

lessons.what_is_taught: Backgrounds, merges, text, and basic tracking in Fusion.
lessons.why_it_matters: Fusion is incredibly powerful for VFX but requires a different mindset than layer-based After Effects.

lessons.what_is_taught: Using the mixer, EQ, compression, and dialogue isolation.
lessons.why_it_matters: Ensures the video sounds as good as it looks.
lessons.what_learner_does: Cleans up dialogue and mixes it with music.

lessons.what_is_taught: Setting up render queues, exporting for web vs broadcast.
lessons.why_it_matters: The final step to getting your work to the client.
lessons.what_learner_does: Finishes the capstone project and renders the final file.
lessons.expected_outcome: A fully finished, graded, and mixed cinematic project.

modules.hands_on_practice: Add VFX and audio mix to the graded capstone project.
modules.assignment: Deliverable: Final cinematic short film edit.
modules.expected_outcome: Mastery of the entire DaVinci Resolve post-production pipeline.
